# URLCode mcp

> Operator-installed declarative MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool server for
> URLCode. Declares bounded tools (name, description, request.body.schema-shaped
> input/output schema, trusted project handler), plus optional bounded
> resources and prompts; the extension owns JSON-RPC 2.0 framing, protocol
> version negotiation, request-id handling, cursor pagination, error codes and
> initialize/ping/tools-*/resources-*/prompts-* dispatch. Installed with
> `urlcode extensions add mcp`; not an independent security assessment. Apache-2.0.

Part of the URLCode framework, in the same repository: docs/FRAMEWORK.md

## What a project declares (YAML only; never packages, code or credentials)
- `extensions.mcp: { version: "1", config: { servers?: { <name>: { mount, serverName, serverVersion, tools: { <name>: { title?, description, annotations?: { readOnlyHint?, destructiveHint?, idempotentHint?, openWorldHint? }, inputSchema, outputSchema?, handler } }, resources?: { <name>: { uri, name, title?, description?, mimeType?, handler } }, prompts?: { <name>: { title?, description?, arguments?, handler } } } } } }`
- A mount for each server, e.g. `/mcp/*: { extension: mcp, methods: [POST, HEAD] }`; the
  client endpoint is the `mount` exactly (`POST https://site.example/mcp`), and `/mcp/` or any
  subpath answers 404 (`/*` is required route syntax, not extra endpoints)
- `auth: true` on a mount to require a session before any tool call runs
- The operator activates it with `mcp()` (optionally `mcp({ onToolError })`) in the site's
  `host.mjs` `composeHost` list; `urlcode extensions add mcp` writes that line and an empty config

## Read in this order
- [README](README.md): server/tool/resource/prompt declaration, handler loading, what is and is not implemented.
- [SECURITY](SECURITY.md): trust boundary, request-id and error-handling guarantees.

## Do not guess
- No JSON-RPC framing, method routing or error-code logic in project
  `function`/`middleware` routes; declare tools/resources/prompts instead.
  Those routes run trusted and in-process, but hold no MCP authority of
  their own.
- A tool/resource/prompt `handler` is trusted project code, runs only after
  arguments pass the declared schema, and must never assume its errors are
  shown to the MCP caller verbatim (they are not).
- A present `Origin` that is not exactly the site's `--origin` answers 403 before parsing; no
  `Origin` is admitted; there is no allowlist of other origins. After `initialize`, an
  unsupported `MCP-Protocol-Version` answers 400 (missing means `2025-03-26`).
- No SSE/streaming transport or session ids in v1 (a core `HandlerResult` has
  no streaming body yet); JSON-RPC batching is refused by design, not
  deferred; see README "What this does not implement".
